The provided evidence from Source [S1] confirms that: 1) Local sampling is inspired by using a ground truth surface representation (depth texture) to place samples around the surface. 2) The paper discusses the limitations of using ground truth depth during inference (memory/computational constraints, need for reprojection). 3) Consequently, the paper targets an 'efficient and compact representation via an MLP-based sampling oracle that only uses ground truth depth during training.' This aligns with the claim's description of using depth oracle networks for local sampling in the context of compact neural radiance fields.
